note: WHICH COLUMNS HAVE ACTUALLY BEEN READ AT MIGNE'S PLATE. Written 2026-08-28, the day 9003's full collation showed our Corpus Corporum Latin departs from the plate at ~3 sites per page against a standing corpus estimate of THREE INSTANCES IN TOTAL. This file exists so that `scripts/plate-gate.mjs` can refuse a [sic:] or a [var:] on a column nobody has read. It records READS, not findings: a range belongs here when someone put the page on screen, read the corner numbers first, and read the running text -- whether or not anything was found. Its opposite number is data/plate-notes/coverage.json, which records only the foot-of-page conjecture layer. || 2026-08-29: extended by the [sic:] plate sweep across PL 113/114/202 — 56 pages, 80 markers, ledger at data/plate-sweep/2026-08-29-sic-sweep.tsv. ⛔ 8988 col 0636A is DELIBERATELY NOT RECORDED: the page was read, but the word (aurursus / aut / au) sits in the extreme right margin where that scan has ink bleed and could not be resolved. Leaving it unrecorded keeps the gate flagging that marker, which is the honest state — a read that could not settle the word is not a read for this purpose.
why_the_gate: A [sic:] asserts a defect in MIGNE'S TYPE and a [var:] asserts that MIGNE'S TEXT diverges from a scriptural witness. Both are public claims about the printed page. Our Latin is not the printed page -- it is Corpus Corporum's transcription of it -- so neither claim can be licensed by the file alone. Corpus frequency detects that an error EXISTS; it cannot say WHOSE it is (reference_plate-read-triage.md). Vulgate collation is worse than useless for the [var:] class: 9003 @0763D showed the digitization MANUFACTURING a divergence (judicabit -> judicavit) that the collation then dutifully 'found'.
rule: NOT A RETROFIT (CLAUDE.md, "RECOVER GOING FORWARD, DO NOT SWEEP THE DONE CORPUS"). The gate is a SHIP TEST: run it on a work before marking it `ours`. Works shipped before 2026-08-28 are surveyed by `--all`, which measures the exposure and exits zero; the number it prints is evidence for a decision about sample width, not a mandate to re-open 38 books.

fields.from/to: inclusive column range, banded (0719A) or bare (0719). A read of one PDF page covers TWO columns, i.e. all eight bands A-D of both.
fields.depth: 'full' = the running text of every column in the range was collated word by word against our Latin. 'read' = the page was read at the plate for a named question and the surrounding text scanned, but not collated word by word. Only 'full' licenses silence about a column; both license a marker, because both mean a human eye met the type.
fields.source: scan identifier + page map + the calibration actually performed. A page map asserted but not calibrated against printed corner numbers is not a source.

8967.scan_defect: INNER-MARGIN CLIPPING: on SOME leaves the left-hand column loses 3-5 characters at the start of most lines (`VERS.` prints as `s.`). ⛔⛔ IT IS SPORADIC AND CANNOT BE PREDICTED FROM THE COLUMN NUMBER. Open the column; never infer. || HISTORY, because the claim was wrong TWICE and each retreat was forced by more reading. (1) At chunking I stated a RULE from five pages: a left-hand column numbered 1 (mod 4) is clipped. (2) Refuted at col 901, and I retreated to 'a strong tendency, 5 of 6'. (3) THAT WAS ALSO WRONG, and by then it was wrong in a way five pages could not have shown. With the reads from cols 0850-0870 in, mod-1 columns stand at 5 CLIPPED (841, 849, 893, 897, 1045) against 6 CLEAN (853, 857, 861, 865, 869, 901). That is a coin flip, not a tendency. ⚑ THE LESSON IS ABOUT THE SAMPLE, NOT THE SCANNER: my five pages were four consecutive leaves plus one, so they sampled one region of one physical gathering and the congruence was an artifact of contiguity. A pattern found in a contiguous sample is a pattern OF THAT SAMPLE until it is tested somewhere else. ⚑ AND THE FAILURE MODE RUNS WHERE NOBODY AUDITS: a wrong 'clipped' does not ship a bad marker, it silently WITHHOLDS a good one and leaves no artifact behind. It blocked three legitimate candidates in cols 0892-0901 before a stint opened the page. || WHAT STANDS: where a column IS actually clipped and a marker rests on a line-opening word, it needs a second copy (Gallica; data/volumes.json) before it may ship.
8967.normalization_class: Corpus Corporum silently conforms Migne's text to the Vulgate. ⛔ INVISIBLE TO EVERY CHECK WE RUN: a Vulgate collation cannot see it, because the digitization has already made Migne agree with the Vulgate. The mirror of the [var:] hazard the runbook records -- there collation MANUFACTURES a divergence, here it DESTROYS one. Only the plate reaches it. Confirmed and patched: 0847A sordescet (TEI had the Clementine's sordescat). Reported, patches pending: 0899B audiebant (TEI has audiebam = Clementine), 0895A populus (TEI has populis), 0866D the TEI INSERTS `vel` before `adipem` (the only one so far that touches sense). Also the hyphenation artifact 0853B de-cidam (TEI has the non-word deeidam). ⭐⭐ AND THE CLASS MUST NOT BE APPLIED BY ANALOGY, which was tested rather than assumed: a SECOND `sordescat` stands at 0869A, and when that leaf was read it prints `sordescat` -- agreeing with our TEI. Patching the twin site by inference would have corrupted Migne's own text into a reading he never printed. Our copy cannot arbitrate this class anywhere.

8999.note: 2026-09-03. All 23 [var:] and all 3 [cj:] of 8999 read at the plate across 23 leaves, BEFORE the work shipped, by six readers working disjoint leaf sets. ⭐ 23 OF 23 [var:] CONFIRMED AS MIGNE'S, ZERO WITHDRAWN; all 3 [cj:] confirmed. No stint fired a [sic:], so nothing could fall. With 9004 (46/46) and 9001 (19/19) that is 88 OF 88 [var:] standing across three Glossa books. 17 TEI patches came instead from the SECONDARY pass over the 19 oddities the stints logged UNMARKED, and from lines read in passing -- not one from a fired marker. ⭐⭐ THE NON-WORD PRIOR DOES NOT HOLD WITHIN A WORK: in cols 381-390 four declined non-words were every one MIGNE'S, while in cols 399-415 five were every one OURS. On 9001 six of six were ours. Same author, same recension, same volume. ⚑ Five of the withdrawals are ONE MECHANISM -- Corpus Corporum mis-rejoining a word Migne broke at a line or column turn (scie-/bat, im-/pleretur, li-/gnis, inter-/rogare) -- found independently by four readers who could not see each other. ⚑ And the read ran in BOTH directions: five sites where CC silently TIDIED Migne's own broken type (contringitur, cupidites, Redit sd, fierit, iu), i.e. where a [sic:] would have been TRUE and our clean file hid it. Full account in src/english/8999/cruces.md; per-reader files in data/plate-findings/.
8999.caveat: ⛔ LEAF n215'S PRINTED RIGHT-HAND CORNER READS 421, NOT 420. Verified at 6x. n216 then reads 421/422, so 421 IS PRINTED TWICE IN PL 114 AND 420 IS NEVER PRINTED -- Migne's compositor mis-numbered the leaf. The running text settles it (n215-right runs VERS. 37 Tu dicis -> Sicut agnus coram tondente, and n216-left opens with that sentence's continuation, our [0421A]), so n215-right IS column 420 and is recorded as such. A reader trusting corner numbers alone would misfile every finding on that column by one. ⚑ ALSO: a <pb> ANCHOR IS NOT A LOCATOR FOR A PHRASE NEAR IT. Four sites in this work sit in a different band from the anchor that precedes them -- actionem personarum is at 386D not 0387A, the [cj:] nobis at 414D not 0415A, liberatum at 0420A not 0420B, Separatur at 0422B not 0422A. This is CLAUDE.md's band-arithmetic false positive seen from the other side and is NOT a defect: the anchors are transcribed where Migne sets them. Nothing was patched.

9000.note: 2026-09-04. All 33 [var:] of 9000 read at the plate across 22 leaves, BEFORE the work shipped: 32 confirmed as Migne's own printing, 1 withdrawn (0307B confusus -> confessus). ⭐ 12 of the 17 TEI patches came from the stints' DECLINED-ODDITY lists or from reading a page opened for something else -- not one from a fired marker, which is John's finding reproduced. FIVE ARE SILENT REPAIRS (CC tidying a defect Migne printed): quator, propetiae lectonis, invenitur- Qoud, sapipientiae, astritus -- the class no collation can reach, because the digitization removed the evidence first; two of them were in no stint's list at all. ⭐⭐ 0330A CONFIRMED AND IT IS A REAL EDITORIAL FINDING: the plate prints Gloria in EXCELSIS Deo at Luke 2:14 and gloria in excelsis again two lines later at Luke 19:38, so Migne (or his source) conformed the nativity song to the entry song the gloss is expounding on that same page. ⚠ SCAN DEFECTS RECORDED FOR THE VOLUME: leaf n153's left corner is set '9 5' (the medial 9 of 295 is a dropped sort), beside the known n215 mis-numbering where 421 prints twice and 420 never. ⚠ The reads are TARGETED, not word-by-word over every column: one reader found in altera species / specie while checking something else and said plainly that a full pass would turn up more of that class. reads.found: Work division page: five stub entries and PROPHETIA BARUCH close above a full-width rule, Matthew opens below it. Archive prints 'ad memorian reliquit'; GALLICA PRINTS 'memoriam' and our twin agrees -- archive-only, refuted, no marker.

Running head confirmed 'GLOSSA ORDINARIA. -- EVANG. MATTH.' FOUR archive-only candidates, ALL REFUTED BY GALLICA, our twin right at each: 'sa cramentum' (split type) vs sacramentum; 'Aminabad' vs Aminadab; 'Eclesiam' vs Ecclesiam; 'ei novissima mors' vs 'et'. Two further archive-only oddities also refuted: 'gentes Domini' (Gallica and Ps 112:4 read Dominus) and 'incipit ad exordio' (Gallica reads 'ab exordio').

CONFIRMED ON BOTH WITNESSES: 'alter in principio sequentis. Sed mystice' -- Migne prints a FULL STOP after sequentis which our twin has lost. TEI patch filed. Gallica's 'tesseratlecadis' is ink; the archive prints tesseradecadis, as our twin does. Archive prints 'generandus.' with a terminal stop at 0067A where Gallica and our twin have none -- archive-only, declined.

Both witnesses confirm the two readings a [var:] rests on: 'Ipse invocavit me' (0069A, perfect for the Vulgate's future invocabit) and 'Ecce Deus adjuvit me' (0069B, perfect for the Vulgate's present adjuvat, beside Migne's own etymology 'Adjutus'). THREE archive-only oddities refuted by Gallica, our twin right at each: 'ressuscitans' vs resuscitans; 'Mathan, qui per Solomonen descendit' vs 'Salomonem'; 'suspicio lector.' vs 'lectori'. Both witnesses confirm the doubled 'Non quod postea convenerint' at 0070C -- it is Migne's, and the two copies have distinct continuations, so it is a splice of two glosses, not an eye-skip.

CONFIRMED ON BOTH WITNESSES: 'sic prophetia non necessitatem EORUM facit' at 0071D, where our twin prints the non-word 'oerum'. Corpus Corporum's corruption; TEI patch filed; the English renders eorum per the PLATE-WHERE-READ rule. Nothing else divergent on either column.

PRESS VARIANT, and the only one in the range: at 0073A Gallica prints the lemma 'Bethehem Judae' (no l) and the ARCHIVE prints 'Bethlehem Judae'. Both are clean, legible, normally spaced; the very next line of both copies prints Bethlehem correctly three times. Our twin follows Gallica's printing. CONFIRMED on both witnesses: @0080B lemma 'Facite ergo fructus dignos', the Lucan plural under a Mt 3 address.

Two archive candidates refuted at Gallica: @0081D 'n on' for 'non' (Gallica sets it closed up) and @0082C 'Inextinguibili' (Gallica prints 'Inexstinguibili', with the s, matching our twin). Also refuted: '(BEDA)' without the internal period at 0084B-style sigla -- Gallica prints '(BEDA.)'. ONE divergence between our twin and BOTH plates: @0081D our twin prints 'Ac si dicat.' where both copies print 'Ac si dicat :'. Filed as a patch.

Two archive candidates refuted at Gallica: @0083C 'cum in quem descendebat' (Gallica: 'eum in quem descendebat', which is also the only reading that construes) and @0084D 'hoc non e st' (Gallica sets 'est' closed up). CONFIRMED on both witnesses: @0084A the lemma is the dative '*Spiritui* Sancto' with only 'Spiritui' in italic, against Mt 4:1's ablative 'a Spiritu'.

One archive candidate refuted at Gallica: @0085A 'non infirmatas fuit' (Gallica: 'non infirmitas fuit'). Nothing else. The Greek at @0086B (λατρεύσεις, λατρεία, δουλεία) is legible and correct on both copies.

The range's strongest-looking archive candidate, refuted in both halves: @0088A archive reads '(ARG.) Quaeritur quomodo Mathaeus et Marcus', Gallica reads '(AUG.) Quaeritur quomodo Matthaeus et Marcus'. Our twin is right on both counts. CONFIRMED on both witnesses and carried as a [var:]: @0087A the lemma 'Habitantibus in regione' against Mt 4:16's 'sedentibus in regione'. CONFIRMED on both: @0087B 'quod clamat in Jordane organo', where the argument wants 'in Joanne'.

THE ONE CONFIRMED DEFECT IN THE RANGE: @0090D our twin reads the non-word 'maledieta'; BOTH plates read 'maledicta'. Corpus Corporum's, filed as a TEI patch; the English renders 'maledicta' per the plate-where-read rule. Two archive candidates refuted at Gallica: @0089A 'altiora virtutem culmina' (Gallica: 'virtutum') and @0089C '(CHRYSOS.)' (Gallica: '(CHRYSOST.)'). CONFIRMED on both witnesses: Migne's own '(Psal. CLXI)' for Ps 141:6.

Three archive candidates refuted at Gallica: @0091B 'dootrina' (Gallica: 'doctrina'), @0092B 'candelabrun crux est' (Gallica: 'candelabrum'), @0092C 'signifi cantia' split across a space (Gallica sets 'significantia' closed up). CONFIRMED on both witnesses: @0091B Migne's conflated Isa 49:6 / Act 13:47, 'Posui te in lucem gentium, ut sis salus mea usque ad extrema terrae'.

Three archive candidates refuted at Gallica: @0093C 'homieidium' (Gallica: 'homicidium'), @0094C 'quadranten novissimum' (Gallica: 'quadrantem'), and @0093D, which mattered most because it would have changed the English -- the archive prints 'si praesens est, *offeres*.' with a comma and a lower-case o, Gallica prints 'si praesens est. *Offeres*.' exactly as our twin has it. Also refuted: 'afferet' (Gallica: 'afferret'). CONFIRMED on both witnesses: @0093A lemma 'Dico autem vobis' against Mt 5:20's 'Dico enim vobis'; @0094B Migne's own contradiction 'ut poenitentiae locum non afferret' immediately followed by 'Sed et locum poenitentiae reliquit'; @0094C Migne's citation '(Marc. XI)' for Mt 5:17.

Four archive candidates refuted at Gallica: @0095A 'silicet' (Gallica: 'scilicet'), @0095D 'per quod jura quilibet veneratur' (Gallica: 'jurat'), @0096A 'ili debet juramentum' (Gallica: 'illi'), @0096A 'Non est po-estas nisi a Deo' with the t lost at the line break (Gallica prints the t). Also refuted: the archive's missing period after the VERS. 31 lemma (Gallica prints '*Det illi.*' as our twin has it). CONFIRMED on both witnesses: @0095B lemma 'Det illi' against Mt 5:31's 'det ei'; @0095A 'Abscinde eam' against the Vulgate's 'abscide eam'; @0095A 'Dextera manus tua' against 'dextra'.

Two archive candidates refuted at Gallica: @0096D '(Math. XI)' (Gallica: '(Matth. XI)', matching our twin) and '(Psal VII)' without the period (Gallica: '(Psal. VII)'). CONFIRMED on both witnesses and marked [var:]: @0096D 'Et maxillam dedi percutienti (Thren. III)' against Clementine Lam 3:30 'Dabit percutienti se maxillam'. CONFIRMED on both and NOT marked: @0096D 'oculum pro oculo, dentem pro dente' without Mt 5:38's 'et' -- this is the Lv 24:20 / Dt 19:21 form, and the gloss is quoting the law, not the evangelist.

ONE CONFIRMED DEFECT IN MIGNE'S TYPE: @0097A 'nomo fidelis' for 'homo fidelis'. Archive at 300 dpi reads 'nomo' unambiguously (initial n, no ascender); Gallica's initial letter is blotted into a closed bowl reading n or o but CARRIES NO ASCENDER AND CANNOT BE h. Our twin carries 'nomo' verbatim, so [sic: *nomo*] is fireable and is fired. FOUR archive candidates refuted at Gallica: @0097A 'victor existas' (Gallica: 'exsistas'), @0097B 'Da ei,' with a comma (Gallica: 'Da ei.'), @0098A 'cum et si' (Gallica: 'cum etsi'), and the whole-word question at @0097D. OUR TWIN'S ERROR, PROPOSED AS A PATCH: @0097D our twin reads 'Ut sitis fiili'; the archive at 600 dpi puts the tall l in third position (f-i-l-i-i) and Gallica reads fili/filii, NEITHER showing our twin's form. CONFIRMED on both and marked [var:]: @0098B 'Sol justitiae non illuxit nobis (Sap. V)' against Sap 5:6 'justitiae lumen non luxit nobis', and 'Super unam civitatem pluit, et non super alteram (Amos. IV)' against Am 4:7.

THE HANDED-OVER LEAD, SETTLED. @0099B the archive prints 'coram homnibus' -- real at 300 dpi, an m followed directly by an n with no dotted i, against dotted i's in 'stitiam' and 'faciatis' on the same line, so NOT a 150 dpi artefact. Gallica f50 prints 'coram hominibus' with the i plainly there, matching our twin. TWO LINES ABOVE, on the same two lines, the archive prints 'haec sententia, supra dixerat' and Gallica 'haec sententia. Supra dixerat' -- a capital/lower-case difference no ink can produce. VERDICT: two printings of PL 114, not two photographs; our twin follows the Gallica printing. NO [sic:] (needs two witnesses, has one) and NO patch (our Latin is correct). One further archive candidate refuted: @0100C 'qui fiilius est' (Gallica: 'filius', matching our twin) -- note this is the OPPOSITE direction from the fiili/filii site on the preceding page. CONFIRMED on both and marked [var:]: @0100C 'Filios genui et exaltavi (Isa. I)' against Is 1:2 'Filios enutrivi, et exaltavi'. CONFIRMED and NOT marked: @0100C 'Vado ad Patrem meum (Joan. VII)', keyed to a chapter containing none of these words -- Migne's locator, passed through under convention 4.

Two archive candidates refuted at Gallica: @0101B 'jure possimus' (Gallica: 'poscimus', matching our twin -- the c is filled with ink) and @0102A 'Quia christus' lower-case (Gallica: 'Christus'). CONFIRMED on both and marked [var:]: @0101B 'Percipite regnum quod vobis paratum (Matth. XXV)' against Mt 25:34 'possidete paratum vobis regnum'; @0102A 'Hic est panis vivus qui de coelo descendit (Joan. VI)' against Jo 6:51 'Ego sum panis vivus, qui de caelo descendi' (the speaker changes); @0102C 'Cum oratis, remittite si quid habetis adversus aliquem: aliter enim Pater vester non dimittet vobis peccata vestra' against Mc 11:25, where a positive purpose clause becomes a negative consequence. CONFIRMED on both and NOT marked: @0100D 'primus' (nominative singular in a first-person-plural clause -- real word, awkward not false); @0102C 'veniam promittit' twice in one sentence (not a doubling: each clause has its own dative).

THE SPURIOUS ASTERISK. @0103C the archive prints what reads as a raised * after 'diebus abstinentiae', immediately before the colon -- Pattern 19's asterisk key exactly -- and the foot of the page carries nothing, which is the shape of a lost note. Gallica prints 'abstinentiae : ut' with a plain colon and no asterisk. NO [cn: * | ...], no [nt:]. Two further archive candidates refuted: @0104A 'VERS. 20.' with a period after VERS (Gallica: 'VERS 20.', matching our twin -- a verse address, and the class 8950 proved cannot be corrected on one witness); @0103D 'in novo Testamento' lower-case (Gallica: 'Novo'). CONFIRMED on both and marked [var:]: @0104A lemma 'Thesaurizare autem' against Mt 6:20 'Thesaurizate autem' -- an imperative printed as an infinitive in a verse-lemma with its own VERS. address; this was NOT flagged by the pre-scan and is the find in this range I would most want a second opinion on. CONFIRMED on both and NOT marked: @0104A 'charitatem amplectantes' (not a form of amplector; treated as an ordinary medieval a/e participle spelling under Pattern 9 -- the strongest non-word candidate in the range that was not fired on); @0104B 'Si etenim illa in genere suo munda tamen sordescit' (verbless si-clause, rendered as an ellipsis).

OUR TWIN'S ERROR, CONFIRMED AND FILED AS A PATCH: @0105C our twin prints 'eleborata' (no Latin word); BOTH copies print 'elaborata' (Gallica line-broken as ela-borata). The English renders what Migne printed. Five archive candidates refuted at Gallica: @0105A 'Quiquid facis' twice (Gallica: 'Quidquid' both times); @0105D 'Animalitas cibe alitur' (Gallica: 'cibo'); @0105D 'invenient eam' (Gallica: 'inveniet'); @0106A 'Et pater vester' lower-case (Gallica: 'Pater'); @0106D 'haec invia sua' (Gallica: 'in via sua', three words). CONFIRMED on both and marked [var:]: @0106B lemma 'Et de vestimentis' against Mt 6:28 'Et de vestimento' -- the launch brief's ⚑ candidate, adjudicated as a real divergence; @0106B lemma 'Si enim fenum agri' against Mt 6:30 'Si autem foenum agri' (connective reversed); @0106C 'Exaudiet me cras justitia mea (Gen. XXX)' against Gn 30:33 'Respondebitque mihi cras justitia mea'. CONFIRMED and NOT marked: @0106A 'Qui sunt hi' against Is 60:8 'Qui sunt isti' -- real but immaterial; @0106B 'fenum' for 'foenum' -- orthography. Printer's signature '4' below the right column on both copies; no notes.

One archive candidate refuted at Gallica: @0107A 'quae mentem pertubant' (Gallica: 'perturbant', matching our twin). CONFIRMED ON BOTH WITNESSES AND MARKED [cj:]: @0107B 'non debet germinari malitia Dei' -- both copies print 'Dei'. The lemma being glossed is 'Sufficit', i.e. Mt 6:34 'sufficit DIEI malitia sua', and the preceding lemma is 'Dies'; the conjecture diei is printed twice on the same page. CONFIRMED on both and marked [var:]: @0107B 'Nocte ac die operabamur ne quem gravaremus (I Thes. II)' against 1Thes 2:9 'nocte ac die operantes, ne quem vestrum gravaremus'. CONFIRMED on both and NOT marked: @0107B 'cura praesenti mentes obruitur' -- plural subject with singular verb; declined because English has no exponent for the concord and the plural noun IS carried into the English ('minds'), so unlike 11632 @0304A nothing is hidden.

9006.note: THE FULL MARKER GATE OF 9006, 2026-08-29, run BEFORE the work shipped. 24 pages rendered at 300 dpi and read by three agents, covering all 37 markers then standing (36 [var:], 1 [sic:]). RESULT: 36 STAND, 1 REVISED, 0 FALSE, 0 UNRESOLVED -- against the 65% false rate PL 114 returned in the [sic:] sweep three days earlier. The difference is the marker POLICY, not luck: this run fired no letter-level type accusations, and nearly every marker is a [var:] on a multi-word scriptural divergence that a single-letter CC misread cannot manufacture. 12 hidden defects of Migne's, silently repaired by Corpus Corporum and invisible to every check we own, were recovered and are patched in data/tei-patches/9006.json.
